Fix: Either show links in the counters line, as the Finished detail already does ('N links not followed'), or remove the Links field and property from ScanProgress.

The classifier is forbidden to name them (TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags), and no test or other source file uses them. They sit in the one file exempt from the reparse rule, which invites exactly the tag-list check SL-043 removed.
key_decisions.rationale:
`git grep -n -E "IO_REPARSE_TAG_(MOUNT_POINT|SYMLINK|DFS)" -- src tests eng` matches only Kernel32.cs:31-33. Tests that need a tag write the literal value.

Its only production caller passes the display root, which NormalizeRoot has already stripped, so both branches are dead in the app and only a test exercises them. key_decisions.rationale:
VolumeSpace.cs:14 (`Extended = @"\\?\"`), :33-34 and :62 do the stripping. LongPath.cs:11 and 31-34 (NormalizeRoot strips `\\?\`) and 61-67 (ToDisplay). Scanner.cs:83 is the only caller: `VolumeSpace.Start(display, _store.VolumeUsedSource, options.VolumeReader, options.VolumeReadBound, options.ReadVolumeOfAnyRoot)`. ScanOptions.cs:24 `VolumeReadBound = VolumeSpace.DefaultBound`. VolumeUsageTests.cs:79 pins `\\?\C:\` → true.
Fix: Have Start and IsDriveRoot take the display root as documented, and drop the prefix handling, or call LongPath.ToDisplay if a Win32 form must be accepted. Make Start's parameters required and let ScanOptions own the default bound.

GetDiskFreeSpaceExW's lpTotalNumberOfBytes is the caller's quota-limited total, while lpTotalNumberOfFreeBytes is the whole volume's free space. Under a per-user quota smaller than the volume's free space, the unsigned subtraction wraps, and the cast turns it into a large negative 'used'. VolumeSpace still reports success. MainWindow.Co…
key_decisions.rationale:
Kernel32.cs:117-125 computes (long)(total - free) with no check that free <= total. The documentation for GetDiskFreeSpaceExW: lpTotalNumberOfBytes 'may be less than the total number of bytes on a disk' under per-user quotas; lpTotalNumberOfFreeBytes is the disk's total free bytes. .taad/slices/SL-043/critique-1.json:103: 'A per-user quota would make TotalNumberOfBytes quota-limited ... so it is not raised.' MainWindow.xaml.cs:550-554 prints a negative volumeInUse as-is. Not reproduced: enabling NTFS quotas needs an administrator.
Fix: Return false (null figure) when free > total. Better, take both numbers from one consistent source, such as GetDiskSpaceInformationW, or FileFsFullSizeInformation's TotalAllocationUnits minus ActualAvailableAllocationUnits.

health_findings.claim: Two modules disagree about what 'file IDs available' means. The Scanner sets FileIdsAvailable from the listing class alone (`!_fullClass`). The store deduplicates per value: HasFileId is false for 0, all ones and the widened 64-bit all ones, and such files are never deduplicated. When a volume answers the extended class but lists files with no ID or a sentinel ID, FileIdsAvailable is true, so MainWindow does not show its note that hardlinks may be counted more than once, yet every hardlinked name is charged in full.
health_findings.evidence:
Scanner.cs:316 `FileIdsAvailable = status != ScanStatus.RootUnreadable && !_fullClass`. ScanResult.cs:54 documents it as 'False when the volume gave no FileIds', which is a statement about values. ScanStore.cs:121-124: the FileId doc says 'as listed: 0 when the volume did not supply one, and possibly one of the "no ID" values HasFileId rules out'. ScanStore.cs:169-170 and 321-328: an entry without an ID is never deduplicated. MainWindow.xaml.cs:457-458 shows the hardlink note only when `!result.FileIdsAvailable`. ListingFallbackTests.cs:29-30 and RootTests.cs:19 test only the class-based cases.
Fix: Derive FileIdsAvailable from the values. For example, count in Scanner.AddEntry the files appended with ScanStore.HasFileId(raw.FileId), and set FileIdsAvailable = that count > 0, or no file lacked an ID. Then the note follows exactly what the store could deduplicate.
(seen by structure)

health_findings.claim: TopLevelKind is a second public enum with the same three members as EntryKind, in a different numeric order: File=0, Folder=1 against EntryKind's Folder=0, File=1. The only link between them is a switch whose default arm maps every other EntryKind to File. A kind added to EntryKind later would become a File row, with Files=1 and Pending=0, while the store's FilesBelow counts only EntryKind.File. The rows would stop adding up to the totals, and only a Debug.Assert would notice. A cast between the enums would turn Folder into File. The App already uses EntryKind directly (FolderTreeNode.Kind), so the second enum does not keep the App away from the store's types.
health_findings.evidence:
EntryKind.cs:4-17: Folder=0, File=1, Link=2. TopLevelSnapshot.cs:6-11: File, Folder, Link. TopLevelTracker.cs:51-56: `_ => TopLevelKind.File`. TopLevelTracker.cs:63-65 derives Files, Folders and Pending from it. FolderTreeNode.cs:4 and 60 use FsAnalyser.Core.Store.EntryKind in the App.
Fix: Make TopLevelRow.Kind an EntryKind and delete TopLevelKind. Failing that, replace the default arm with explicit arms and a throw for an unknown kind.
(seen by structure)

health_findings.claim: used = (long)(total - free) subtracts two different figures. GetDiskFreeSpaceExW's lpTotalNumberOfBytes is the caller's quota-limited total, while lpTotalNumberOfFreeBytes is the whole volume's free space. Under a per-user quota smaller than the volume's free space, the unsigned subtraction wraps, and the cast turns it into a large negative 'used'. VolumeSpace still reports success. MainWindow.Coverage then shows 'The volume reports -526,133,493,760 bytes in use; this scan counted ... more than that.' FormatSize prints negatives as raw bytes. The SL-043 critique noted that the total becomes quota-limited under a quota, but not that the difference can go negative.

MainWindow.xaml.cs:550-554 prints a negative volumeInUse as-is. Not reproduced: enabling NTFS quotas needs an administrator.
